desired_outcome: A recruiter uploads a CV PDF and receives a structured skills matrix in under 60 seconds, with each skill tagged by proficiency level (beginner/intermediate/expert) and grounded in a quoted CV sentence.

candidates.design_context_override: favor explicit user gates over implicit automation

b1_output.agreed_solution_description: A FastAPI service accepts a CV PDF, extracts text via pdfminer, passes the text to Claude for skills extraction with a structured tool schema (skill_name, proficiency_level, evidence_quote), and returns a JSON skills matrix. A React table renders the matrix grouped by proficiency tier.

architecture_decisions.rationale: Deterministic, no external API calls, handles multi-column CVs.

architecture_decisions.choice: Claude tool-use with a three-level schema (beginner/intermediate/expert)
architecture_decisions.rationale: The three levels match the recruiter's stated requirement. Structured output guarantees valid enum values.

ux_decisions.choice: Drag-and-drop PDF upload with progress indicator
ux_decisions.rationale: Recruiter workflow is file-centric; drag-and-drop reduces friction vs. file-picker button.
ux_decisions.discovery_anchor: A recruiter uploads a CV PDF

abstraction_test.reasoning: Components: PDFExtractor, SkillsClassifier, SkillsMatrixView. Names convey roles.

responsibility_alignment_test.reasoning: Each component owns one concern: text extraction, classification, display.

evolution_test.notes: If PDF library changes, only PDFExtractor changes. If proficiency schema expands to 5 levels, only SkillsClassifier prompt changes.

communications_patterns_test.notes: One-way: Upload → PDFExtractor → SkillsClassifier → SkillsMatrixView. No cycles.

data_connectedness_test.notes: Each stage receives complete data from upstream.

data_variations_test.notes: Non-PDF upload → rejected at upload gate. Empty CV → returned with empty skills matrix and a warning. PDF with no text (scanned image) → returns extraction_error with guidance to use OCR.

assumptions: CVs are machine-readable PDFs (not scanned images) in v1
Proficiency classification accuracy does not require human review in v1

discovery_anchors.excerpt: grounded in a quoted CV sentence

candidates.design_context_override: minimize new abstractions — reuse existing patterns

b1_output.agreed_solution_description: Reuse the existing FastAPI backend. Add a /skills-matrix endpoint that accepts PDF bytes, extracts text, and calls Claude Opus with a structured skills schema. The frontend adds a new tab to the existing BMC canvas with the skills matrix table.

architecture_decisions.choice: New /skills-matrix route in the existing FastAPI app
architecture_decisions.rationale: Avoids a second service. Reuses existing Claude client configuration and error handling.

ux_decisions.choice: New tab in existing canvas UI
ux_decisions.rationale: Keeps the recruiter in one tool.
ux_decisions.discovery_anchor: A recruiter uploads a CV PDF

abstraction_test.reasoning: SkillsMatrixEndpoint and SkillsMatrixTab are role-clear names.

responsibility_alignment_test.reasoning: The endpoint is handling both extraction and classification — two distinct responsibilities. A future change to the extraction library would also touch the classification logic inside the same function.

evolution_test.notes: Splitting extraction from classification later would require refactoring the endpoint. The folded responsibility is a known tech debt assumption.

data_connectedness_test.notes: Endpoint receives PDF bytes. Has all it needs.

data_variations_test.notes: Same as c1 but with an additional assumption: the existing BMC canvas frontend is stable enough to add a tab without regressions.

assumptions: The existing BMC canvas frontend is stable enough to add a tab
CVs are machine-readable PDFs in v1
Extraction and classification can be folded into one function without maintainability issues
